journey.name: Offline — failures must not look like an empty library
journey.description:
Pubky is the only source of truth and there is no local cache, so a network failure has to read as "we can't reach your homeserver", never as "you have no decks". Before the fix, `DeckRepositoryImpl.listByAuthor` swallowed transport failures into an empty list and both Home and Decks rendered their empty states — indistinguishable from having lost everything.
Requires a signed-in session (journey 01) and at least one published deck. Turn the radios off with: adb shell svc wifi disable && adb shell svc data disable and back on afterwards with `enable`.

actions.action: With wifi and mobile data disabled, force-stop and relaunch the Loopky app
Verify the Home tab shows an error state with a title and a retry action (resource-id: error_retry), NOT the "Nothing to study yet" empty state and NOT a "Create a deck" call to action
Verify the error message does not contain any raw URL, "HTTP transport error", or other FFI diagnostic text
Verify the Decks tab also shows an error with a retry action, NOT "No decks yet"

Verify the profile still shows the identity and the Decks/Cards counts this device last saw, with an em dash under "Due" — a listing that could not be read must never be reported as three zeros, which reads as "my decks are gone"
Re-enable wifi and mobile data, then tap the element with resource-id "error_retry"
Verify the deck list loads and the previously published decks are shown
